subject: RFI: Replica scaling and raw throughput validation for tokenized LLM workloads
messages:
From: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@globex.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Arun Menon <arun.menon@globex.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: throughput validation and replica scaling for tokenized workloads

Hi Tessa / Marissa,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. As part of our procurement tracks for critical LLM infrastructure, the SRE and platform teams at Globex need a clear, reproducible answer to two related questions:

1) For our typical inference mix (average prompt 120 tokens, response 320 tokens, 8 concurrent requests per user), what steady-state aggregate throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec) can Redwood sustain for a single model replica on your Dedicated offering, and how does that map to tail latencies (p95/p99) at 95% CPU/GPU utilization?

2) How does horizontal scaling behave under realistic traffic ramps and sudden bursts — specifically how many replicas are needed to maintain p99 < 300ms for the user-facing tail when QPS increases 5x over a 30s window, and what is your autoscale recovery profile?

Please provide: test methodology (drivers, warmup, traffic shape), exact runtime / model config used (batching, quantization, KV cache warm), the raw logs or artifacts produced by the run, and any scripts or config we can use to reproduce on our testbed.

We attached a short starter spreadsheet with our target mixes (bench-parameters.xlsx). Ideally we can turn this around before our architecture review the week of May 24.

Thanks,
Priyanka Shah
Lead Platform Engineer, Globex Corporation

Attachment: bench-parameters.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: throughput validation and replica scaling for tokenized workloads

Priyanka —

Appreciate the detail in the spreadsheet. We can absolutely provide a reproducible lab run and raw artifacts. Proposed plan (high level):

- We will run three scalar experiments: steady-state throughput (per-replica), burst ramp (5x over 30s) and degraded node scenarios (replica eviction/fallback).
- Test harness: open-source driver (we use a fork of locust with a token-aware driver that replays prompt/response lengths and enforces prefix cache patterns). We will also provide the driver script (run-driver.sh) and the exact invocation in the shared Drive.
- Warm-up: 10 minutes or 10k requests, whichever comes first. Steady-state window: 30 minutes.
- Metric collection: per-request latencies, GPU utilization (sampled at 5s), batch sizes, and KV cache hit ratio.

I attached a proposed matrix for the runs (proposed-matrix.csv). Ben and Karthik will add runtime knobs — Ben, can you confirm which quantization and batching profiles we'll run by default?

I'll schedule a 45-min sync tomorrow to walk through the artifacts with your SREs.

—Tessa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-matrix.csv (csv stub)

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@globex.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: throughput validation and replica scaling for tokenized workloads

Folks — adding details on the runtime matrix and a short summary of observed numbers from our internal lab so Globex has concrete expectations. Full raw results and scripts will be shared to the Drive link after the run.

Runtime/config notes (defaults for this run):
- Model: open-llm/rosetta-13b (float16), served via Redwood Dedicated runtime
- Instance: nv24 (2xA10-like GPUs) isolated pool
- Batching: dynamic batching with max_batch_size=64, preferred_batch_ms=8
- KV cache: enabled; we populate with representative prefix set during warm-up
- Quantization profile: 16-bit float for primary; we can provide 8-bit quantized variant in a separate run
- Autoscale policy used for burst test: scale out at 70% GPU util sustained for 30s, scale in after 3m below 40%

Summary lab numbers (single model replica steady-state; synthetic driver replaying Globex mix):
- Steady-state (1 replica): 520 reqs/sec, ~2200 tokens/sec; p50=38ms, p95=112ms, p99=260ms; GPU util ~72%
- 4 replicas (horizontal): aggregate 2000 reqs/sec, aggregate tokens/sec ~8500; per-replica p99 ~270ms (slight variability due to cross-replica batching alignment)
- Burst ramp (5x over 30s) with autoscale enabled: observed transient p99 spike to ~900ms for 18s while new replicas came up, dropped under 300ms within 55s after scale completion when caches warmed on new replicas
- Degraded node scenario (single replica OOM + eviction): graceful fallback to next-compatible variant occurred; tail latency for impacted requests spiked to 1.2s for ~40s while in-flight traffic drained and routing completed

Repro methodology notes (important differences from naive tests):
- We maintain per-request token sequencing to exercise KV cache steady-state; naive uniform random prompt lengths underestimates real-world latency because it prevents cache reuse between related sessions.
- We sample and expose batch size distribution as part of artifacts rather than only mean throughput — that helps validate cost/efficiency tradeoffs.

Attachments we will drop in Drive after today's run: runtime-configs.yml, run-driver.sh, and a gzipped archive of per-request logs (redwood-benchmark-results-20270512.tar.gz). Let us know if you need raw GPU traces (nvidia-smi logs), we can include those too.

—Ben
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment references: runtime-configs.yml, run-driver.sh, redwood-benchmark-results-20270512.tar.gz (stubs)

Thanks, Ben/Tessa — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we run the artifacts against our verifier:

- For the burst test, can you provide the exact scaling latency (time from threshold breach to first traffic served by new replica) and the size of the boot image (GB) you used for the replica boot? We need to model cold boot time into our availability plan.
- For degraded node behavior: did you observe any request reordering or duplication when in-flight traffic was rerouted?

Also, we will need the raw per-request log and the exact run-driver invocation so our testbed yields comparable results. Please drop those into the Drive link and mark the file names in your response.

—Priyanka

Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: throughput validation and replica scaling for tokenized workloads

Priyanka —

Answers inline and next steps: 

- Scaling latency: time from 70% sustained GPU util to first successful response from new replica in our lab averaged 32s (stddev 4s) for nv24 images using our pre-baked boot image (compressed ~1.1GB, uncompressed ~3.4GB). For cold-starts from scratch on a warm host it was ~18s. We include boot image size and checksums in runtime-configs.yml.
- Reordering/duplication: we instrumented request IDs; we did not observe duplication at the application layer. A small fraction (<0.03%) of requests were returned out-of-order for streamed responses while connection handoffs occurred — those were retried by the driver; we recorded the retries in the per-request log.

Artifacts dropped to Drive: run-driver.sh, runtime-configs.yml, redwood-benchmark-results-20270512.tar.gz (contains per-request CSV, batch-size histogram, GPU util series). Full nvidia-smi traces and kernel-level dumps available on request — we'll share through a secured transfer.

Next steps: I'll schedule the 45-min sync for Friday May 14 10:00am PT to walk through the artifacts and go over reproducibility on your side. If Globex wants a turnkey run inside your VPC (private deployment), we can provide an execution plan and a time estimate for a one-off validation engagement.

Thanks,
—Tessa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: links to Drive files (run-driver.sh, runtime-configs.yml, redwood-benchmark-results-20270512.tar.gz)
